messages:
alex: Heads-up — running into a weird Expo/metro issue when importing our JS SDK in a fresh RN app. Bundler errors: "Unable to resolve module 'stream' from .../node_modules/redwood-sdk/dist/index.mjs". SDK is built ESM-only.
marie: Are you on Expo managed or bare? Metro treats ESM differently.
sam: Managed. Expo SDK 48, metro config mostly default. 
alex: Managed (Expo Go). Tried adding "resolver.extraNodeModules" fallbacks for stream -> stream-browserify, crypto -> react-native-crypto, but then hit RN polyfill headaches and bundle size exploded.
jess: Oof. Two things to try: 1) publish a CJS entrypoint + conditional exports for react-native, 2) add a tiny shim package that re-exports only the shimmed pieces (stream, crypto getRandomValues).
marie: Also check package.json "exports" field. Metro doesn't follow conditional exports well for ESM-only packages. If you provide a "main" (cjs) and "module" (esm) it helps older bundlers.
sam: For a workaround I patched node_modules with rn-nodeify style shims and added a metro.config.js: 
```
const defaultConfig = require('expo/metro-config');
const config = defaultConfig(__dirname);
config.resolver.extraNodeModules = { stream: require.resolve('stream-browserify') }
module.exports = config;
```
But that felt too fragile for our customers.
alex: The other major pain is typings. TS complains because our SDK's types use NodeJS types (ReadableStream etc.) and RN TS project doesn't have those libs. Lots of errors about "Cannot find name 'ReadableStream'".
jess: You can publish separate types for react-native via publishes: e.g., typings-rn.d.ts and add "types": "dist/index.d.ts" and maybe a "types:react-native" convention — but npm doesn't support conditional types well. Another approach: ship DOM/stream friendly types that avoid NodeJS-only symbols.
marie: Can we instead make the SDK build target a tiny RN-compatible bundle under dist/rn/, and add a "react-native" field in package.json pointing to it? Metro will prefer that field. That lets us keep ESM for web/node while providing RN-specific entry that uses polyfills we control.
sam: That sounds ideal. Then sample app import is the same: import { Redwood } from 'redwood-sdk' and metro picks react-native entry.
ajex: (typo) alex: +1 to react-native field. Also add quickstart notes for Expo: explain which polyfills to include and mention that Expo Go still lacks some Node polyfills so we should recommend using a minimal shim bundle.
jess: One more gotcha — Hermes's RNG. If the SDK uses subtle crypto or relies on Node getRandomBytes, we need to fall back to expo-random or react-native-get-random-values. Add runtime detection: if (typeof crypto?.getRandomValues !== 'function') { require('react-native-get-random-values') }
sam: I can prototype dist/rn rollup that replaces streams with simple async iterators we control (we don't need full Node stream semantics for token streaming).
marie: Excellent. Also open a docs PR with a checklist: package.json entries (react-native, main, module), RN-specific bundle, recommended polyfills, TS guidance (add lib: ["es2020", "dom"] or add a small ambient types file), and a sample Expo app that demonstrates using the RN entry.
alex: Created a tiny repro repo and linked it in the ticket: https://github.com/redwood/repro-rn-sdk-esm (private). Will add sample app once rollup is ready.
dev-bot: Reminder — RFC #248 (sdk-rn-entrypoints) draft assigned to @jess, due in 5d.
marie: Cool. If we do react-native entry + typings fix we can mark SDK as "Expo-friendly" in the docs. Also call out known caveats (managed Expo Go vs custom dev clients).
jess: I'll own the RFC + a small CI test that builds the sample Expo app on CI to catch regressions. Thanks team.
alex: Thanks — saved us from shipping a broken DX to early users.
